# 888 URL to Markdown (888-url2md) API — Full Documentation

> High-performance Web Reader, Live Web Search (SERP), Document & PDF Parsing (Firecrawl AnyDoc), and Multi-URL Batch Crawling API service for LLMs and AI Agents. Converts web pages, document files (PDF, Word, Excel, PPT, EPUB, RTF, CSV), and live search queries into clean Markdown or structured JSON.

---

## 1. Capabilities Overview

1. **Single URL Web Reader & Scraper**: Convert any web page or online document URL into clean LLM-friendly Markdown.
2. **High-Speed Document & PDF Parsing (AnyDoc Engine)**: Extract and convert local document files (PDF, DOCX, DOC, XLSX, XLS, PPTX, PPT, EPUB, RTF, ODT, ODS, ODP, CSV) into clean Markdown with sub-5ms latency via multipart form-data or direct remote URLs.
3. **Real-Time Live Web Search (SERP)**: Execute zero-config live web searches and get structured Markdown snippets powered by DuckDuckGo with multi-engine fallback.
4. **Multi-URL Batch Crawling**: Fetch, scrape, and convert multiple web pages concurrently in a single HTTP request with isolated fault tolerance.
5. **Image OCR & Text Extraction (PaddleOCR PP-OCRv4 Engine)**: Convert image files (PNG, JPG, JPEG, WEBP, BMP) and screenshots into clean Markdown or line-level bounding box JSON with multi-node failover pool and anti-thundering-herd protection.
6. **Flexible Response Formats**: Supports clean GitHub-Flavored Markdown (`Accept: text/plain` or default), structured JSON (`Accept: application/json`), or SSE event streaming (`Accept: text/event-stream`).
7. **WebMCP Browser Tools**: For Chrome browsers supporting WebMCP (`document.modelContext`), automatically registers `search_web`, `read_web_page`, and `read_web_pages` client tools.
8. **Adaptive Structured Extraction**: Opt-in CSS selector relocation with bounded, origin-scoped profiles and ambiguity rejection.
9. **Resumable Deep Crawling**: Bounded concurrency, optional per-domain AutoThrottle, and checkpoint resume for asynchronous jobs.
10. **LLM-Friendly Waiting**: Explicit synchronous timeout budgets and async job polling guidance prevent duplicate crawler work.

---

## 2. API Endpoints & Detailed Usage

### 2.1 Single URL Reading
- **GET Request**: `/<URL>`
  *Example*: `/https://news.ycombinator.com`
- **POST Request**: `/`
  *JSON Body*:
  ```json
  {
    "url": "https://news.ycombinator.com"
  }
  ```

### 2.2 Document & PDF Parsing (AnyDoc Engine)
- **Direct Online Document URL**:
  - `GET /https://arxiv.org/pdf/2301.00001.pdf`
  - `POST /` with `{"url": "https://example.com/document.docx"}`
- **Multipart Form-Data File Upload**:
  - `POST /`
  - Form field `file` or `pdf`:
    ```bash
    curl -X POST "https://<HOST>/" \
      -H "Accept: text/plain" \
      -F "file=@sample.pdf"
    ```
- **Supported Formats**:
  - PDF (`.pdf`)
  - Microsoft Word (`.docx`, `.doc`)
  - Microsoft Excel (`.xlsx`, `.xls`)
  - Microsoft PowerPoint (`.pptx`, `.ppt`)
  - EPUB e-books (`.epub`)
  - Rich Text Format (`.rtf`)
  - OpenDocument Formats (`.odt`, `.ods`, `.odp`)
  - CSV / Tabular Data (`.csv`, `.tsv`)

### 2.3 Live Web Search (SERP)
- **Path-based Search**: `GET /s/<QUERY>`
  *Example*: `/s/artificial+intelligence` or `/s/%E5%8F%B0%E7%A9%8D%E9%9B%BB`
- **Query Parameter-based Search**: `GET /search?q=<QUERY>`
  *Example*: `/search?q=NVIDIA+stock`

### 2.4 Multi-URL Batch Crawling (Batch Crawl)
- **POST Request**: `/v1/batch` (or `/batch` or `/`)
  *JSON Body*:
  ```json
  {
    "urls": [
      "https://example.com/page1",
      "https://example.com/page2",
      "https://example.com/page3"
    ]
  }
  ```

### 2.5 Image OCR & Text Extraction (PaddleOCR PP-OCRv4 Engine)
- **POST Request**: `/api/ocr` or `/v1/ocr`
- **Multipart Form-Data File Upload**:
  ```bash
  curl -X POST "https://<HOST>/api/ocr" \
    -H "Accept: text/plain" \
    -F "file=@screenshot.png"
  ```
- **JSON / Base64 Body**:
  ```json
  {
    "image": "data:image/png;base64,..."
  }
  ```
- **Supported Formats**: PNG, JPG, JPEG, WEBP, BMP, GIF.
- **Upload Size Limit**: Up to 50MB per file (supports ultra-high resolution screenshots, multi-megapixel scans, and uncompressed PNGs; reverse proxy configured for 50MB, internal engine up to 100MB).
- **Optional Query Parameters**:
  - `lang`: `ch` (default, PP-OCRv4 bilingual Chinese & English) or `chinese_cht` (Traditional Chinese).
  - `use_angle_cls`: `true` (default) / `false` (orientation angle auto-detection).
  - `mode`: `table` (isolates and returns ONLY the reconstructed table, stripping editor chrome/footers).
  - `table_only`: `true` (alias for `mode=table`).
- **2D Spatial Table Reconstruction & Isolated Tables**:
  The OCR engine clusters 2D bounding boxes and detects horizontal and vertical gutters in tabular data, outputting clean, ready-to-render GitHub-Flavored Markdown (GFM) tables directly (`| Header 1 | Header 2 |...`). JSON responses include `data.tables` (an array of isolated table strings).
- **Pure Frontend (SPA) Direct Access (CORS)**:
  Full browser CORS is enabled (`Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`, credentials for trusted origins, preflight OPTIONS). Client-side SPAs (React, Vue, Vite, BlockNote) can invoke `/api/ocr` directly from the browser:
  ```typescript
  // Upload table image and insert into BlockNote editor
  async function insertOcrTable(editor: BlockNoteEditor, imageBlob: Blob) {
    const fd = new FormData();
    fd.append('file', imageBlob, 'table.png');
    // Using ?mode=table strips surrounding editor noise
    const res = await fetch('https://<HOST>/api/ocr?mode=table', {
      method: 'POST',
      headers: { 'Accept': 'application/json' },
      body: fd
    }).then(r => r.json());
    const tableMd = res?.data?.tables?.[0] || res?.data?.markdown || res.markdown;
    const blocks = await editor.tryParseMarkdownToBlocks(tableMd);
    editor.insertBlocks(blocks, editor.getTextCursorPosition().block, 'after');
  }
  ```
- **Service Capabilities & Health Check**:
  - `GET https://<HOST>/api/capabilities`: Probe dynamic OCR cluster status (`data.ocr.available`, latency, nodes).
  - `GET https://<HOST>/api/ocr/status`: Inspect active node and cluster health.

---

## 3. Response Formats

### 3.1 Plain Text / Markdown (`Accept: text/plain` or default)
Returns clean GitHub-Flavored Markdown. For batch requests, pages are separated by `---`.

### 3.2 Structured JSON (`Accept: application/json`)
```json
{
  "code": 200,
  "status": 20000,
  "data": [
    {
      "url": "https://example.com/page1",
      "title": "Page 1 Title",
      "content": "# Page 1\n\nContent here..."
    }
  ]
}
```

---

## 4. Optional Headers & Customization

| Header | Values | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `X-Respond-With` | `markdown` \| `html` \| `text` \| `frontmatter` | Output format selection (default: `markdown`) |
| `X-Preset` | `reader` \| `index` \| `research` \| `agent` \| `spider` | Extraction preset configuration |
| `X-Target-Selector` | CSS Selector string (e.g. `article`, `main`) | Focus extraction on matching DOM elements |
| `X-Remove-Selector` | CSS Selector string (e.g. `nav`, `footer`, `.ad`) | Remove unwanted elements from DOM before conversion |
| `X-No-Cache` | `true` \| `false` | Bypass internal cache and force live fetch |
| `X-Timeout` | Integer `1`–`180` | Browser rendering timeout in seconds (default: dynamic, recommended: `15`–`30`+) |
| `X-With-Generated-Alt` | `true` \| `false` | Enable AI-generated image captions |
| `X-With-Images-Summary` | `true` \| `false` | Include image metadata summaries |
| `X-With-Ocr` | `true` \| `false` | Opt into OCR text & table extraction for documents (auto for scanned PDFs) |
| `X-Content-Filter` | `pruning` \| `bm25` | Filter noisy DOM blocks or score relevance via BM25 |
| `X-Content-Query` | String query | Search query string used with BM25 filter |
| `X-Session-Id` | String UUID/ID | Persist and reuse browser session cookies across requests |
| `X-Detach-Invisibles` | `true` \| `false` | Detach display:none elements from DOM snapshot |
| `X-Adaptive` | `true` \| `false` | Enable conservative adaptive CSS structured extraction |
| `X-Adaptive-Id` | Safe identifier | Select the persisted adaptive profile |
| `X-Adaptive-Threshold` | `0.5`–`0.95` | Set the minimum adaptive candidate confidence |

---

## 5. Advanced Crawling & Extraction Options (JSON Payload)

When calling `POST /` or `POST /v1/batch`, the JSON payload supports advanced crawler options:

### A. CSS / XPath Structured Data Extraction (Zero-Token Cost)
Extract deterministic JSON fields directly without LLM inference:
```json
{
  "url": "https://example.com/products",
  "extraction": {
    "type": "css",
    "baseSelector": ".product-card",
    "fields": [
      { "name": "title", "selector": "h3.title", "type": "text" },
      { "name": "price", "selector": ".price", "type": "number" },
      { "name": "link", "selector": "a.buy-btn", "type": "attribute", "attribute": "href" }
    ]
  }
}
```
The response returns `data.extracted` containing the structured JSON array.

Adaptive relocation is CSS-only and opt-in. The first successful extraction stores bounded element signatures per origin and identifier; later requests can relocate missing selectors only when the candidate is sufficiently confident and unambiguous:

```json
{
  "url": "https://example.com/products",
  "adaptive": true,
  "adaptiveId": "product-card",
  "adaptiveThreshold": 0.7,
  "extraction": {
    "type": "css",
    "baseSelector": ".product-card",
    "fields": [{ "name": "title", "selector": "h2" }]
  }
}
```

### B. Fit Markdown / BM25 Content Filtering
Reduce LLM prompt token costs on large documents by filtering irrelevant boilerplate or scoring relevance:
```json
{
  "url": "https://example.com/long-article",
  "contentFilter": "bm25",
  "contentQuery": "quarterly revenue profit"
}
```
The response returns `data.fitMarkdown` containing only the relevant sections.

### C. Bounded BFS Deep Crawling
Crawl linked pages within the same domain with conservative limits:
```json
{
  "url": "https://docs.example.com/intro",
  "deepCrawl": {
    "maxDepth": 2,
    "maxPages": 10,
    "maxDurationMs": 30000,
    "includePatterns": ["https://docs.example.com/*"],
    "concurrency": 3,
    "concurrencyPerDomain": 2,
    "autoThrottle": true
  }
}
```

`concurrency` is capped at 20 and `concurrencyPerDomain` at 10. The default remains sequential. `autoThrottle` adjusts per-domain delay from response latency and 403/429 blocked responses.

### C.1 LLM Wait and Polling Contract

- Normal synchronous pages: client timeout **15–30 seconds**.
- Dynamic JavaScript or anti-bot pages: client timeout **30–45 seconds**.
- Deep crawls and document conversion: client timeout **45–60 seconds or more**; use `asyncJob: true` when the task can exceed the client budget.
- Do not submit duplicate POST requests before the timeout expires. A client-side retry can create duplicate browser sessions and a thundering-herd load spike.
- For an async job, wait for the initial acceptance response, save the `jobId` and private `accessToken`, then poll `GET /jobs/{jobId}` every **2–5 seconds** with `X-Job-Token`.
- End polling at `completed`, `failed`, or `cancelled`. An HTTPS webhook can notify completion, but polling remains the recovery path if delivery fails.

### D. Asynchronous Job Queue & HTTPS Webhooks
For long-running deep crawls or background processing:
```json
{
  "url": "https://example.com",
  "deepCrawl": { "maxPages": 20 },
  "asyncJob": true,
  "webhook": {
    "url": "https://my-service.com/webhook"
  }
}
```
Returns a `jobId` and `accessToken`. Poll progress with `GET /jobs/{jobId}` using the `X-Job-Token: <accessToken>` header, cancel via `POST /jobs/{jobId}/cancel`, or resume a cancelled job via `POST /jobs/{jobId}/resume`.

The response is wrapped in the standard envelope. The identifiers are at `data.id` and `data.accessToken`:

```json
{
  "code": 200,
  "status": 20000,
  "data": {
    "id": "crawl_...",
    "status": "running",
    "accessToken": "...",
    "statusUrl": "/jobs/crawl_..."
  }
}
```

Use this exact sequence:

1. Send one `POST /` with `asyncJob: true` and `deepCrawl`.
2. Poll `GET /jobs/{data.id}` every 2–5 seconds with `X-Job-Token: {data.accessToken}`.
3. Read state from `data.status` and the completed crawl from `data.result`.
4. Stop at `completed`, `failed`, or `cancelled`.
5. Use `POST /jobs/{data.id}/cancel` to cancel, poll until `data.status` is `cancelled`, then use `POST /jobs/{data.id}/resume` to resume, with the same token.

Avoid these errors: cancel/resume are not `GET`; cancel acknowledgement may precede the `cancelled` state; the token is not the job ID; the token must not be placed in the URL; and the original POST must not be duplicated while the job is running.

## 6. WebMCP Browser Tools

When the web UI is opened in a WebMCP-compatible browser (Chrome with `document.modelContext`):

```javascript
// Available tools
document.modelContext.registerTool({
  name: "search_web",
  description: "Search the live web and return results as Markdown.",
  inputSchema: {
    type: "object",
    properties: { query: { type: "string" } },
    required: ["query"]
  }
});
```

---

## 7. Tool Specification (LLM / Agent Schema)

```json
{
  "name": "888_url2md",
  "description": "Fetch and convert web pages, document files (PDF/Word/Excel/PPT/EPUB/CSV), search results, or multiple URLs into clean Markdown.",
  "parameters": {
    "type": "object",
    "properties": {
      "urls": {
        "type": "array",
        "items": { "type": "string" },
        "description": "List of web page URLs to scrape concurrently in batch."
      },
      "url": {
        "type": "string",
        "description": "Single web page URL to scrape, document URL, or search query."
      }
    }
  }
}
```

## 8. Crawler Timeout Sizing & Cascading Fallback Architecture (Thundering Herd Warning)

### 8.1 The Risk: Premature Timeouts & The Thundering Herd Problem (驚群效應)
When building AI Agent, LLM, or RAG search pipelines, architects frequently chain multiple web scrapers in a fallback cascade (e.g. `888-url2md` ➔ `Jina Reader` ➔ `Crawl4AI`, or vice versa).

If the client or gateway router sets an overly aggressive timeout (such as 3–5 seconds) for the primary crawler:
1. **Premature Abort**: Complex web pages (heavy React/Vue SPAs, dynamic client-side hydration, Cloudflare/anti-bot challenge verification, network latency) often legitimately require 8–20 seconds to load and parse. A 3–5s timeout will prematurely kill valid requests that were close to finishing.
2. **Cascading Failover Storm**: When multiple concurrent requests timeout nearly simultaneously in the primary tier, they all immediately fail over to the subsequent tier at the exact same moment.
3. **Thundering Herd Collapse**: The final fallback tier is suddenly inundated with a synchronized spike of heavy, slow-rendering requests. This exhausts its Puppeteer/Playwright browser pool, triggers rate limits or token budget exhaustion, spikes server load, and causes end-to-end failure across the entire pipeline.
4. **Wasted Compute**: Earlier scraper tiers may continue headless rendering in the background for abandoned requests, multiplying server CPU and RAM consumption across all participating nodes.

### 8.2 Recommended Timeout Budgets
- **Standard HTML Web Pages**: Configure client HTTP timeout and `X-Timeout` header to at least **15s – 30s**.
- **Dynamic JavaScript / Single Page Applications (SPAs)**: Set timeout to **30s – 45s** to allow DOM mutation and network idle settling.
- **Deep Crawling / Document Uploads**: Set timeout to **45s – 60s+**, or decouple execution via `asyncJob: true` and poll `/jobs/{jobId}` or use HTTPS webhooks.

### 8.3 Multi-Crawler Orchestration Best Practices
- **Generous Primary Budget**: Give the primary crawler at least 20–30s before considering a fallback.
- **Staggered Retries with Jitter**: When falling over to Jina, Crawl4AI, or 888-url2md, apply randomized exponential jitter (e.g. `base * 2^attempt + rand(100ms, 800ms)`) to de-synchronize request waves.
- **Circuit Breaker**: If a domain consistently times out across multiple requests, trip a domain-level circuit breaker instead of flooding fallback engines.
- **Explicit Timeout Header**: Pass `X-Timeout: <seconds>` (max 180) to inform 888-url2md of the intended server-side rendering budget.
